newsitem.title: INDIA: New India ministers shun ill-starred oath date.
newsitem.headline: New India ministers shun ill-starred oath date.

text.p: India's head of state delayed the induction of new ministers into the government on Wednesday after they pleaded that the timing -- eight days after the full moon -- was inauspicious.

Government officials said four south Indian politicians, including former finance minister P. Chidambaram, did not want to be sworn in on Wednesday as it fell on "ashtami", the eighth day after the new or full moon.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma, who had scheduled the oath-taking ceremony for Wednesday evening, agreed to put it off for a day until 6 p.m. (1230 GMT) on Thursday, an aide said.
Many Indian politicians and citizens consult astrologers before arranging schedules. Few Hindus would schedule a wedding or start a new job without first visiting an astrologer.
Ashtami, which marks the eighth day after the start of a lunar fortnight, is considered an unpropitious time to embark on a new enterprise. Hindus in south India pay special attention to the date.

Sharma was expected to induct Chidambaram and three others from his Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) party into Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's government. The TMC is based in the southern state of Tamil Nadu.
